Answer: B
Reason: The CT images (Figures 1a-1c) demonstrate diffuse, randomly distributed micronodules throughout the lung parenchyma, which is the hallmark radiographic appearance of miliary tuberculosis. This pattern correlates strongly with the clinical history of prolonged fever and increased sedimentation rate, whereas the other options describe distinct patterns (e.g., peribronchovascular for sarcoidosis, centrilobular for inhalation) not seen here.
